With the L-8 fix the in-process quit now also usually restores the task itself before the process ends (session result 'Stopped: Forerunner was closed. "X" is ready to continue.').

fixed.how: Root cause: CriticService.modelReview called driver.run without the review's signal; the critic's run was stopped only through its kill-switch registration under the task, which exists once the run started. Now the critic's run gets ctx.signal (packages/critic/src/critic.ts), review() throws 'killed' before running anything when its signal is already aborted, the runtime's critic port (loop/critic.ts) goes no further after the page try once aborted, and the runner registers the review's controller before the task moves to in_review (a move between the run's end and that transition is recorded as a move during the run instead of failing the session).

blocking.issue: The chat's cancel read-back (new in this branch, L-10/L-7) promises 'what it changed is removed' for a task that has a pull request, while the cancel keeps the pull request and its work. moveAsk never looks at pr_url, but the actual outcome (personMove's work = task.pr_url ? 'pull_request' : 'removed') and the row's Cancel dialog (cancelWorkLine: 'Its review stops now; its pull request stays open.') do. Every task of a repository (GitHub) project carries pr_url from the end of its run, before it goes to review (runner.ts:1522 patches pr_url, then the in_review transition). So 'skip the X task' or 'cancel the X task' on such a task while it is being reviewed (or rerun after a rework) reads back a removal that never happens. This is the L-7 class this area fixes, it breaks design §5 rule 9 ('No promises the code does not keep'), and it contradicts the fixer's claim that the read-back is worded the same way as the row's Cancel dialog.

fixed.how:
There were two root causes.

First, intake-content.ts PROMISE read any 'I/we will give/send/provide/share <X>' as content handed to Forerunner, whoever received it. It also judged an item by its last word, so 'a REST API with JSON data' counted because it ends in 'data'. Now handedToForerunner sorts each promise:
- It counts when it names Forerunner: 'give you', 'provide you with', 'send … to you', 'share … with you'.
- It also counts when the person ('I', 'we', the owner, the client) promises it and names no one else, unless it uses 'can' or 'share' or is ongoing work ('weekly', 'every day').
- It does not count when it goes to someone else ('send subscribers a …', 'give them …', '… to members', 'provide members with …') or when a customer promises it.
- An item now counts by its head noun, the words before a preposition ('photos' in 'photos of the garden'). 'members' and 'team' are no longer content words.

Second, intake.ts:1172 applied withOwnersContent to every redraft from the original brief, so the person's change never won. withOwnersContent(proposal, brief, changes) now checks the person's changes with the new dropsOwnersContent. If a change drops the step or refuses to give, using words like drop, remove, leave … out, nothing, no or not together with content, the first task, asks me, questions, give or an item, the model's redraft stands, and later changes do not bring the step back. Any other change ('Make the headings blue.') keeps the step.

The redraft is now told the plan the person read, one line per task, with the person's questions (IntakeDraftOptions.read via planRead, taken from the answered card). The Change the plan answer and Try again after a restart both pass it, so 'drop the first task' names a task the model knows, even one the code added. fixed.how: New packages/runtime/src/loop/try-plan.ts (planTries) decides what to try from the brief, the criteria, the README the task wrote and its files. A command is used only when it is written exactly: in backticks, in a code block, or in a sentence whose next word carries the sentence on. The program must be node, python3 or python, with the script in the folder. Placeholders become sample input under .forerunner-try/ (<file> becomes a 2-line, 9-word text). A file that listens is a server: its documented start command or `node <file>`, its documented GET routes first, then the routes its code handles. A tool whose usage nobody wrote down, a missing script and a <url> are 'not tried, because…' lines. New packages/runtime/src/loop/try-run.ts (runTries) runs them in the review's sandbox lease: the container when Docker is ready (always for a full review), else the process sandbox, network off, 30 s per command and 15 s to listen. A server runs through a small driver script inside the same sandbox, which starts it, waits for it to listen, calls it over loopback and kills it. Nothing is started on the host without a sandbox. A failing command, a crash, a 5xx or a 4xx on a named route is a blocking measured finding ('Tried <target>: <problem>'). A server nobody asked to run that fails (it needs a database) is told, not held against the task. .forerunner-try/ and any files the try wrote are removed. critic.ts opens the lease for checks or tries. fixed.how: The driver now starts the server through a guard: the same script with --guard and the argv in FR_TRY_ARGV. The guard leads its own process group (detached on POSIX), runs the server as its child in that group, and keeps its standard input as a pipe from the driver that is never written. When the driver ends, however it ends, the pipe closes and the guard kills its whole group: the server and whatever it started. When the server ends by itself, the guard writes its exit or spawn error after @@FR-GUARD@@ on standard error and kills the server's leftover children. The driver reads the report at the guard's 'close', so exit codes and 'python3 is not installed' are reported as before. On Windows the sandbox's taskkill /T takes the driver's whole tree, and the guard uses taskkill when its pipe closes. In the container, timeout -s KILL kills the driver and the guard does the rest; the lease's destroy removes the container in any case. runTries throws the stop (stopIfAborted) before and after each try, so the runner handles it as a stopped review.
